body.statement: If \(D^{\circ}\neq\varnothing\), the infimum and supremum of \(b\) over \(\mathcal M_{+}\) equal \(L\) and \(U\). The lower endpoint is attained in \(\mathcal M_{+}\) if and only if some \(z\in C_{\theta_U}\cap D^{\circ}\) satisfies \(b_{\theta_U}(z)=L\); the upper endpoint is attained if and only if some \(z\in C_{\theta_L}\cap D^{\circ}\) satisfies \(b_{\theta_L}(z)=U\).
body.justification: Strict log-odds models can lose endpoint attainment at marginal contacts even when their closure has the same bounds.
body.gap: CiocaneaTeodorescuGabrielSjolander2025 assumes positive cells; the exact closure-to-strict transfer and finite attainment criterion under assay uncertainty are not given there.
body.consumer: Software and applied reports can distinguish an attained sharp bound from a merely approachable sensitivity limit.
body.proof_tex:
Assume \(D^{\circ}\neq\varnothing\), and fix \(z^{\circ}\in D^{\circ}\).  Since \(D\) is convex, for every \(z\in D\) and \(0<t\leq1\),
\[
 z_t=(1-t)z+t z^{\circ}\in D^{\circ}.
\]
Indeed, the two strict inequalities defining \(D^{\circ}\) hold for \(z_t\) because they hold at \(z^{\circ}\) and weakly at \(z\).  Thus \(D^{\circ}\) is dense in \(D\).  A channel lies in \(D^{\circ}\) exactly when both corrected margins lie in \((0,1)\).  For finite \(0<\theta<\infty\), the sign argument in the unique-root proof is then strict at both Fr\'echet endpoints, so the compatible root is strictly inside that interval and all four cells are positive.  Conversely, four positive cells force both margins into \((0,1)\).  Hence \(D^{\circ}\times[\theta_L,\theta_U]\) is precisely the channel--odds domain generating \(\mathcal M_+\).

Continuity and density now give
\[
 \inf_{\mathcal M_+}b=min_{\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cl}}}b=L,
 \qquad
 \sup_{\mathcal M_+}b=max_{\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cl}}}b=U.
\]
For attainment of the lower endpoint, suppose first that some \(z\in C_{\theta_U}\cap D^{\circ}\) satisfies \(b_{\theta_U}(z)=L\).  The attaining-law construction has four positive cells by the preceding paragraph and therefore belongs to \(\mathcal M_+\); this proves sufficiency.  Conversely, suppose a strict law attains \(L\).  Its four cells are positive, so
\[
 \frac{\partial b}{\partial\theta}<0.
\]
Consequently its odds coordinate must equal \(\theta_U\).  Its channel is a minimizer in \(D^{\circ}\).  If \(q_0\neq q_1\), the finite-envelope proof excludes an interior stationary channel.  A strict boundary minimizer cannot lie on a marginal-contact edge; on an axis-aligned edge it is a vertex or a stationary-line contact, and on the informativeness edge it is a vertex or its unique stationary point.  It is therefore in \(C_{\theta_U}\cap D^{\circ}\).  If \(q_0=q_1\), the only additional possibility is the ridge \(u+v=2q_0\); its intersection with \(D\) has a boundary representative with the same value, and every point on that ridge has corrected margins \(p_0=p_1=1/2\), so that representative remains in \(D^{\circ}\) and belongs to the candidate map.  Degenerate polygon cases use the same edge argument.  Necessity follows.  Replacing minimum by maximum and \(\theta_U\) by \(\theta_L\) proves the upper-endpoint criterion.
